title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - D-2
notes:
West leads the ♠J against 1NT. There are 5 top tricks (2 spades, 2 hearts, and the ♦A). South's long clubs will provide more than enough tricks for the contract once the ♣A and ♣K are dislodged. South must make the correct play at trick 1, however, or the contract will be in danger.

If South makes the natural "second hand low" play and wins the ♠K in the closed hand and then starts on clubs, the defense will duck the first round of that suit. West will win the second round of clubs and continue spades to drive out dummy's ♠A. South will have only 1 entry back to his hand (the ♥K) which will not be enough to establish the clubs and then later enjoy them.

South can always make 1NT, but he must win West's spade opening lead with dummy's ♠A in order to preserve the ♠K as an entry to the closed hand. South should start clubs by leading dummy's ♣Q and now it will not help the defense to duck this trick (or to win it for that matter). West wins the second round of clubs and plays a second spade to South's ♠K.

With the lead conveniently placed in the South hand, clubs can be established by knocking out the remaining honor. West is welcome to cash his 3 spade winners, but South will later by able to get to his hand with the ♥K in order to enjoy 3 more club tricks. South will actually end up with an overtrick as a result of his careful play to the first trick.
